text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA

- New round of negotiations with London Club of creditors opens in Belgrade. Yugoslavia's debt to commercial banks estimated at $2.4 billion. Creditors rejected Yugoslavia's proposal for its debt to be reduced by 80 percent due to deteriorated state of its economy.

- Bosnian Serb member in the Bosnian collective presidency Momcilo Krajisnik invites Hague war crimes investigators to Pale to question former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic, charged for genocide in Bosnia.
- Democracy only path to Europe, says British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook in interview to Radio B92.

- Main reason for insolvency of Montenegrin companies is huge accumulated claims. Firms from Serbia owe Niksic steel works 18 million dinars while its outstanding debts are 1.5 million dinars, says steel works director Miodrag Perovic.
- Shortages of petrol at private petrol stations. Owners call on the state to allow imports of oil derivatives so they should not depend solely on Serbia's oil company NIS.
- Monetary expansion in June has still not negatively reflected on stability of prices and dinar exchange rate, says Economics Institute of Belgrade.
- Montenegrin Trade Minister Branko Vukovic said Serbian financial police and interior ministry disrupting flow of goods between the two republics.
- "Investigation is an insult for my people," says Moslem National Council of Sandzak leader Sulejman Ugljanin.
POLITIKA
- Agreement on equal representation of political parties on Serbian radio-television during election campaign signed in Serbian government. Main opposition parties boycotted meeting.
- July retail prices 0.1 percent up on June. Inflation since the start of the year 3.3 percent, says Federal Statistics Office.
BORBA

- More than 400 road construction and other capital projects in Serbia to be financed by the Serbian government from real sources. Around 900 million dinars to be secured from sales of oil derivatives and 550 million dinars from the Serbian Development Fund, says Serbian minister without portfolio Dejan Kovacevic.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --

- "The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia is our choice and not something we are forced into. We do not want a passive role in Yugoslavia because we do not think Yugoslavia is strengthened that way," said Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
- A delegation of The Hague War Crimes Tribunal is expected to visit Montenegro in September at the invitation of Montenegrin state prosecutor Vladimir Susovic.
- Koni clothing manufacturer from Niksic signs deal with Italian firm Agam, expected to bring it annual income of around 700,000 German marks per year. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4305
